q: “Talk to the baby in your belly, WHY AREN’T YOU TALKING TO THE BABY??” “Don’t dance too much at the wedding!” “Don’t lift anything heavy, stop moving so much” (real unsolicited comments I’ve gotten)
cx: First-time mother, introvert, worn out by comments at family events.

q: I also obviously know how to start preparing for my own baby, but no one believes you know how to do anything yet.
cx: 30-year-old first-time mother on being treated as if she can't function.

q: constantly answering the “How are you feeling MAMA” question & insane inquiries about whether or not I’m breastfeeding is getting tiring, especially when they end with, “YOU HAVE TO, IT’S BEST FOR THE BABY.”
cx: Questions she gets at every family function.

q: I can only do so much ranting to my husband since he’s not the pregnant one fielding these questions
cx: Why she posted to strangers.

q: I just don't know where to look or where to just start.
cx: Found out she was pregnant at 12 weeks with no symptoms.

q: My parents now have my coffee because it's my kryptonite. Both of them told me I could drink one a day but then realized I have been drinking way more caffeine lately.
cx: What her parents did after she learned she was pregnant at 12 weeks.

q: We booked everything before knowing I was pregnant and our hotels have open bars right in the nightlife area and all I want is to sleep early. I want so bad to experience this with my husband and we have done so much, I just feel like I’m ruining everything and I’m just so tired. :/
cx: Seven months pregnant at the end of a long trip to Japan.

q: Now I’m two months postpartum, exclusively breastfeeding, running on broken sleep, and trying to bond with my new little family — and last week alone, I had thirteen house guests come through.
cx: Moved to her hometown at 8 months pregnant for family support; possibly tool-polished post, one voice.

q: My mom comes almost every day, but that’s because she helps with the baby and gives me a window to sleep in the mornings — it’s not a dinner, it’s not a hangout, it’s survival.
cx: Separating her mother's help from social visits.

q: My extended family drives two and a half hours to visit and stays for four hours at a stretch, while I’m nodding off mid-conversation. There was even a comment early on — “are we allowed to come over yet?” — just a month after we’d moved in
cx: Visitors from both sides almost every week.

q: It’s a tender subject because it’s his family, and what often happens is that it turns into a comparison — he’ll point out that we see my family more, and suddenly it becomes a one-up thing instead of a real conversation.
cx: Trying to raise visitor overload with her boyfriend.

q: I don’t have a reference point for what a healthy, sustainable cadence of family time looks like — especially with a newborn, especially as someone who needs space to function.
cx: Away from home for ten years before moving back.

q: I’ve always taken a lot of pride in my hygiene so I’m just flabbergasted and flummoxed at this point at the strength of the scent.
cx: 25 weeks, a body change she had never heard about.

q: Now I believe I was entitled to some paid time off, since I haven't asked for any of that previously, but instead of time off, my manager swapped my shifts so now I have to work 4 long nights in a row, which sounds unreasonable.
cx: UK night worker at 20 weeks asking for an antenatal appointment for the first time.

q: But most of all... I miss being able to eat without knowing it's about 50/50 chances of throwing it back up. It's honestly ridiculous.
cx: 30 weeks, sickness from the first trimester now replaced by heartburn.

q: My clinic insisted it was normal and nothing to worry about. They did not appreciate me repeatedly pointing out how much weight I lost because of it lol.
cx: First-trimester sickness; she changed clinics after moving.

q: So much of the media portrays it as “oh, you’re a little more hungry when you’re pregnant and you’ll want weird things!” but that isn’t it AT ALL and some days it feels so discouraging. I feel like a bottomless pit
cx: 10 weeks with first baby, hunger plus aversions.

q: Counting down the days to the second trimester when I hope things will look up by changing a bit
cx: 10 weeks, the joy gone from eating.

q: My hospital recommends packing a baby blanket for delivery. Is that for the car ride home? Or am I missing something? Not sure if I need to buy a baby blanket
cx: Hospital packing list item nobody explained.

q: Sadly no one gifted swaddle blankets. I have 7 muslin blankets/swaddles and ordered one Love to Dream swaddle to try, and I figured if baby won’t go with either of those we will panic buy other swaddles after birth 😅 Do you think that’s enough?
cx: Giving birth in June in a hot, dry climate.

q: I miss my body so much. Not in a body image sense, but just a comfort sense. Everything is still so uncomfy.
cx: About two weeks after the birth of her son.

q: How I can't rock, bounce or carry my baby the same way my husband can. How I can't sit or lay down while holding my baby for too long.
cx: Two weeks postpartum, limited by recovery after a hard delivery.

q: of course he wants mom and I’m a big sucker and he’s been miserable so I’ve been taking care of him almost exclusively
cx: 38 weeks, nursing a sick 7-year-old days before a planned birth.

q: Some women had been waiting over 9 hours for a booked appointment, I can acknowledge they’re understaffed, but I’m surprised at how small the triage is. I had my past two children at hinchingbrooke hospital
cx: UK, third pregnancy, new area, worried about her new hospital.

q: Hi I never ended up transferring myself as all the hospitals around have the same CQC rating for maternity wards, so it made sense to just stay put where it’s closer xx
cx: Update weeks later on switching hospitals.

q: I'm barely sleeping and I'm worried about entering the newborn trenches already the most exhausted I've ever been in life.
cx: 38 weeks, itching and pain keeping her awake.

q: It appears that according to regulations I can only get 2 weeks off after birth. The semester will end mid December and the classes are Monday to Thursday 17.00 till 20.00. I do plan to get a part-time nanny to help in those hours
cx: Due in October, accepted to a masters starting in August.

q: Thank you everyone for your opinions, I have decided to forego the program for now because it seems it will be too stressful.
cx: Her decision after replies.

q: He said at first that there aren’t many options to switch right now but if I did switch, I would be losing out on a lot of money for my family.
cx: Construction project manager at 23 weeks with a 16-month-old; asked at 10 weeks to switch roles.

q: I would still check my phone and see I got a text at 3 pm from my boss asking me to complete something by 5pm that day. I didn’t do it.
cx: While on PTO because she and her toddler were sick.

q: I am scared I am going to get fired and half of me wants to quit. I am working 8-11 hour days most days, I have an hour commute one way
cx: 23 weeks, falling behind on emails.

q: My husband does not have medical insurance through his work, so I feel completely trapped.
cx: Why she can't quit the job.
